skill.name: learn-reset
skill.description: Reset a learning knowledge base to a clean state after explicit user confirmation.
skill.summary: Clears learned patterns, cache data, session notes, and learning state while preserving the knowledge directory structure.
skill.author: 0xrdan

security_audit.summary: All 13 static external-command findings are false positives caused by markdown inline backticks and fenced example blocks, not executable code. I found one semantic concern: the skill clears knowledge files and resets state. Accidental use can cause data loss despite confirmation.

remediation.issue: Destructive reset can remove accumulated knowledge.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, show target files and counts, and recommend a backup or commit before reset.

remediation.issue: Reset scope depends on the assistant following the documented paths.
remediation.suggestion: Keep reset operations limited to the documented knowledge files and report every changed file after completion.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Knowledge Reset
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to clear accumulated knowledge files and reset state. It asks for confirmation, but successful use can permanently remove local assistant learning data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The destructive behavior is explicitly documented in the warning and reset instructions. Confirmation reduces accidental use but does not remove data-loss impact.

content.value_statement: Accumulated learning files can become stale or noisy over time. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a confirmed reset that preserves the file structure.
actual_capabilities: Prompts the assistant to request confirmation before resetting knowledge files.
Clears learned patterns, quirks, and decisions while keeping the file structure.
Clears the classification cache and current session context.
Resets learning state values such as extraction count and query counters.
Provides a completion summary with counts of cleared entries.
limitations: It cannot recover cleared entries after confirmation.
It does not remove old knowledge from git history.
It only describes the reset workflow; the assistant performs file edits.
It assumes the expected knowledge directory and files already exist.

use_cases.title: Start A Clean Learning Cycle
use_cases.description: Reset noisy learning data before collecting new patterns for a project.

use_cases.title: Remove Stale Project Notes
use_cases.description: Clear old decisions and quirks after a major refactor or architecture change.

use_cases.title: Prepare A Shared Workspace
use_cases.description: Empty personal learning state before handing a workspace to another contributor.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Reset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use learn-reset to clear the learning knowledge base. Ask me to confirm before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Reset With Counts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use learn-reset and report how many patterns, quirks, decisions, and cache entries were cleared.

prompt_templates.title: Reset Before New Phase
prompt_templates.prompt: Use learn-reset after confirmation, then leave the knowledge structure ready for a new project phase.

prompt_templates.title: Audited Reset Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use learn-reset with a careful review. Show the files you will clear, wait for confirmation, reset them, and summarize the final state.

output_examples.output: The assistant asks for confirmation, clears learning entries after approval, resets state, and reports the number of cleared items.

output_examples.input: Clear stale learning notes before the next sprint.
output: The assistant lists the reset targets for review.
After confirmation, it clears patterns, quirks, decisions, cache, and session context.
It finishes with a short reset summary.

output_examples.input: Start fresh but keep the knowledge folders.
output_examples.output: The assistant preserves the knowledge directory structure and replaces learned content with empty baseline files.

best_practices: Review the learning files before confirming a reset.
Keep project backups or git commits before clearing knowledge.
Run the reset when starting a new phase or after noisy learning has accumulated.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill when you need to preserve historical insights.
Do not reset without explicit confirmation from the workspace owner.
Do not assume it removes old content from repository history.

faq.question: Does this skill delete the knowledge directory?
faq.answer: No. It preserves the directory structure and clears selected learning content.

faq.question: Will it ask before changing files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to request confirmation before resetting knowledge.

faq.question: Can cleared knowledge be restored?
faq.answer: Only if you have a backup, commit, or other saved copy.

faq.question: Does it clear git history?
faq.answer: No. Previous commits may still contain old knowledge.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when accumulated learning data is stale, noisy, or no longer useful.
